ask: Design the /roadmap skill: what it reads in a repo, how the page is laid out, and how merges update a step's status.
note: Shows, per repo: every debt and note, your feedback items and where each went, the repo's plans, each session's plan, and open PRs and branches. The page reads each item from its one home, stores no copy, shows when it last read, and marks what it could not read as unknown. Needs feedback items homed in the repo first. Session pages (live, o10) sit under the repo page (lasting). Your idea, Oct 22: a live view with pixel-art workers showing each one's state; it draws from records sessions already write, read when the page opens, with no new watcher (c26). Where each worker's live state comes from is still open. Your rule, Oct 21: the page is a current record, not a log; this roadmap's own upkeep now runs through c55 (the triage thread and build.py's upkeep list), which a repo page can copy. Your pick, Oct 22: B, logbook (claude.ai/artifact/9H4NgQdoNNhU939mXojVv9), with your UI changes started; A and C unused. Each themes per repo from one block of tokens. Merged in from o7 (triage, Oct 26): the page also shows the repo's map, the session-board mod's progress and compliance-check scores, as one health view.
title: Give every repo a living roadmap page
why: The process behind this page, made repeatable: audit the repo, turn the findings into phased steps with a plain why and an ask for each, publish one page per repo, and update it in place as lanes land. A /roadmap skill in claude-settings would build it from docs/plans and docs/debts, and the merge step would tick off the steps it completes. It pairs with the health view: health shows how the repo is, the roadmap shows what's next.
